feedback.body: Thabo, you evaluated the expression strictly from left to right without following the rule that multiplication and division should be done before addition and subtraction. This led to an incorrect answer. To improve, practice solving expressions by first doing all multiplication and division before moving on to addition and subtraction, regardless of their position in the problem. This will help you get the correct results.

Nomsa, when you add fractions, you need to make sure the pieces you're adding are the same size. You added the top numbers and the bottom numbers separately, which isn't correct. Try cutting paper strips into equal pieces to see how fractions add up when the pieces are the same size. This hands-on activity will help you understand why you can't just add numerators and denominators directly.

Ravi, you treated negative numbers as if they were positive when ordering them, which led to mistakes. To understand this better, try drawing a number line and marking where negative numbers like -8 fall, moving left of zero. Also, when adding decimals, you misaligned the decimal points, which changed your answer. Next, practice drawing a line through the decimal points before adding and fill in any empty spaces with zeros to keep the numbers properly aligned.

Fatima, it looks like you are reading the percentage sign as a decimal point, and you are adding the tops and bottoms of fractions separately. Remember, percent means out of one hundred, so you should divide by 100 first when working with percentages. For adding fractions, try cutting two strips of paper into different numbers of equal pieces and see how you can only add pieces that are the same size. This hands-on step will help you understand how to add fractions correctly.

Chen, in your work, you subtracted numbers when simplifying fractions instead of dividing both the top and bottom by the same number. Simplifying means splitting into equal groups, so the next step is to practice dividing the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor. Also, when comparing decimals, you looked only at the digits after the decimal point without considering the whole number, which can be misleading. Try writing both decimals with the same number of decimal places and then compare them digit by digit.

Kwame, you made some mistakes with brackets and the way you added fractions. Remember, everything inside the brackets should be worked out first as one value before moving on. You also added the tops and bottoms of fractions separately, which is not correct. Try using paper strips cut into equal parts to see how to add fractions properly.

Amira, you made a small mistake when converting a number to a percentage, but your method was correct. Please try multiplying again carefully to get the right percentage. Also, when adding fractions, you added the tops and bottoms separately, which is not quite right. Try cutting two paper strips into equal pieces and see how you can combine them only when the pieces are the same size before adding.

Grace, you made some mistakes when rewriting the expression because you left out the brackets, which can change the meaning. Remember to carry the brackets down each step until you have worked out the value inside them. Also, when subtracting a negative number, think of it like taking away a debt, which actually adds to the total. Lastly, when dividing the total amount, add all the parts of the ratio first to find the total shares before dividing, not just the number of parts named.

Ibrahim, you wrote a fraction where a mixed number was asked for and added numerators and denominators separately, which is not the correct method. Also, when multiplying, the decimal point was moved the wrong number of places. To improve, try cutting two paper strips into equal pieces of different sizes and practice adding the pieces to understand how to add fractions properly. This hands-on activity will help you see why the pieces must be the same size before adding and help with your understanding of fractions.

Sofia, you worked through the problem from left to right without following the rule that multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction. Also, when simplifying fractions, you subtracted instead of dividing both the top and bottom by the same number. The next step is to practice the order of operations by doing all multiplication and division before addition and subtraction, and to simplify fractions by dividing numerator and denominator by their common factors.

Daniel, when you rewrite expressions, it's important to keep the brackets until you fully simplify what is inside them. Also, when you find a common denominator for fractions, remember to multiply both the top and bottom numbers by the same amount. This keeps the fractions the right size and helps you add them correctly. Try practicing carrying brackets through each step and scaling both parts of the fraction when you change the denominator.
